- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent dip, but true outcome shows sharp drop or mean reversion, adjust downward by 3–8% for next 5–10 days.
- After a price spike (forecast > 70), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.3) and price is falling, model often underestimates drop; add 1–3% buffer below true low to avoid under-shock.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates > 5% from model in first 5 days, apply “lag correction”: subtract 1–2% per day for remaining forecast horizon.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.5), model tends to overfit short-term noise; use 10-day smoothed average as anchor for correction.
- If true outcome shows “double dip” (fall, then rebound), model often misses second dip; forecast should reflect 2–3 day lag in rebound phase.
